title: Pilgrimage Road in Jerusalem
summary: An Aramaic inscription that likely contains the earliest extra-biblical reference to the 'House of David'.
historical_context: Important for the history of Israel, Aram-Damascus, and debates over dynastic language.
ancient_near_east_context: The item belongs to the broader imperial, cultic, and urban world of the ancient Near East and the biblical periods reflected in the dataset.
literary_context: Frequently discussed in connection with Davidic dynasty references in Kings and Samuel.
covenantal_significance: Pilgrimage Road in Jerusalem helps anchor biblical claims in historical reality while reminding readers that archaeology supports rather than replaces interpretation.
interpretive_notes: The inscription is genuine, but the reconstruction and interpretation of damaged lines remain debated.
Use the item as context for the biblical text, not as a shortcut around it.
